name: esp2026_seat_set
story: Each back reclines 5 degrees and comes back up, one seat after another; the aisle armrests lift 90 degrees for access; then the tray tables fold down level and stow again.

steps.title: Open the Dynamic Simulation environment
steps.command: Environments tab > Begin panel > Dynamic Simulation
actions: Open esp2026_seat_set.iam in Inventor.
Click the Environments tab, then Dynamic Simulation.
steps.note: Dynamic Simulation works out how an assembly moves, and the forces and speeds as it moves.

steps.title: Turn constraints into joints
steps.command: Dynamic Simulation tab > Manage panel > Simulation Settings
actions: Click Simulation Settings and tick Automatically convert constraints to standard joints. Click OK.
Open Standard Joints in the browser to see the joints Inventor made from your assembly constraints.
steps.note: Parts held together with no movement between them become one rigid group, listed under Welded group.

steps.title: Check the recline joints
steps.command: Dynamic Simulation tab > Joint panel > Insert Joint
actions: In Standard Joints find the Revolution joint for each back: the back lugs on the recline pivot pins.
Every part fixed to a back (shell, cushion, cover, head rest, screen, power module, pocket, tray arms, latch) should be in one Welded group with it.
steps.note: A revolution joint lets the back turn about the pivot axis and nothing else: one degree of freedom.

steps.title: Join the recline locks
steps.command: Dynamic Simulation tab > Joint panel > Insert Joint
actions: Each lock needs three joints. Insert Joint, Revolution: the lock eye on the front pin in the bracket.
Insert Joint, Cylindrical: the rod in the bore of the lock, so it can slide.
Insert Joint, Revolution: the rod eye on the rear pin in the back lever.
steps.note: Locked, the hydraulic valve stops the rod sliding, so the back is held. The recline button opens the valve.

steps.title: Join the armrests and trays
steps.command: Dynamic Simulation tab > Joint panel > Insert Joint
actions: Insert Joint, Revolution: each armrest on its pivot pin.
Insert Joint, Revolution: each tray table on its hinge stubs.

steps.title: Drive the backs
steps.command: Right click a back Revolution joint > Properties > dof 1 (R) > Edit imposed motion
actions: Tick Enable imposed motion. Drive: Position.
Seat 1: 0 at 0.5 s, 5 degrees (fully reclined) at 2.5 s, hold to 5.5 s, back to 0 at 7.5 s.
Seats 2 and 3: the same, half a second and a second later: each passenger chooses for themselves.
steps.note: The back reclines from 12 to 17 degrees from vertical: 5 degrees of recline, inside the 3 to 6 the brief allows.

steps.title: Check the recline lock stroke
steps.command: Dynamic Simulation tab > Joint panel > Insert Joint
actions: Right click a lock Cylindrical joint > Properties and look at dof 2 (T): Inventor works out how far the rod slides as the back reclines.
Pin to pin: 353.9 mm upright, 345.1 mm reclined, a stroke of 8.8 mm.
steps.note: Choose a lock with at least this stroke: a 20 mm stroke lock leaves room to spare.

steps.title: Lift the armrests, lower the trays
steps.command: Edit imposed motion on the armrest and tray joints
actions: Aisle armrests: 0 at 9 s, 90 degrees up at 10.5 s, hold, down again by 13.5 s.
Trays: 0 at 14 s, 78 degrees (level) at 15.8 s, hold, stowed again by 19.4 s.
Click OK twice.
steps.note: The armrest lifts clear of the seat, so a passenger can slide across from an aisle wheelchair.

steps.title: Run the simulation
steps.command: Dynamic Simulation tab > Manage panel > Simulation Player
actions: In the Simulation Player set Final Time to 20 s and Images to 1000.
Click Run. The assembly moves and the timeline fills in.
Use the slider to scrub back and forth.
steps.note: Press Play below to run the same motion here.

steps.title: Plot the results
steps.command: Dynamic Simulation tab > Results panel > Output Grapher
actions: Open the Output Grapher.
Under Standard Joints, tick the angle of each back, lock and armrest joint, the position of the lock Cylindrical joints and the tray angle.
The graph shows each value against time. Click on the graph to move the simulation to that moment.

steps.title: Record a video
steps.command: Dynamic Simulation tab > Manage panel > Simulation Player
actions: In the Simulation Player click Record (the red dot) and choose a file name and format.
Click Run again. Inventor saves a video of the motion for your portfolio.
steps.note: You can also export a moment to Stress Analysis (Export to FEA) to check a part at its highest load.
